subject: Post-call: NovaApps evaluation — next tests & capacity questions
messages:
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: sara@novaapps.com, tim@cloudpros.io
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: NovaApps evaluation — next tests & capacity questions

Hi Sara / Tim — thanks for a great call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary of what we heard
- NovaApps: productionizing a multi-tenant recommendation endpoint, 99th p99 latency target ~120ms at 50 RPS steady with 100 RPS bursts.
- Key concerns: predictable tail latency during burst, cost vs GCP committed use, and ability to fall back to smaller models without code changes.

Proposed focused tests (suggested order)
1) Latency + burst simulation (our infra): 50 RPS steady / 200 RPS 30s bursts, measure p50/p95/p99 and kv-cache hit-rate. (We can run in hosted sandbox with a dedicated pool.)
2) Reserved-capacity trial (Dedicated): 7-day reserved pool sized to your peak (estimate 4xA100 equivalent). Validate capacity guarantees + failover to regional backup.
3) Hyperscaler parity run: run same workload on GCP A3/TPU+ ephemeral to compare raw throughput, queuing behavior, and egress costs.
4) Cost projection & quality regression: run 10k request prompt set (your representative prompts) and capture token counts and output diffs.

What we'll provide
- A benchmark_spec.csv (attached) with exact load profiles and logging keys.
- A canary run playbook for Dedicated -> fallback policies.
- A one-page cost model comparing redwood Dedicated vs typical GCP committed-use and on-demand scenarios.

Action items / owners
- Diego (me): schedule latency + burst run; provide cost model draft by EOD Friday.
- Tim: share any procurement constraints (minimum term, required PO wording).
- Sara: confirm a 10k prompt set (or point to sample prompts) and preferred 7-day window for reserved pool.
- Marissa: lead contract/procurement touchpoint once NovaApps signals intent.

Attachments: benchmark_spec.csv (CSV, 3 KB)

If that looks right, I’ll schedule the latency run for next Tuesday and loop in infra.

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0187

Sara — quick notes from pricing/procurement side:

- Trial commitment: for a 7-day reserved pool we typically run it as a timeboxed evaluation with no long-term monetary commitment (we cover infra allocation for the trial). If you convert the reservation into a monthly Reserved Capacity contract, standard terms are 3/6/12 month commitments — pricing scales with term and capacity.
- SLA: Dedicated customers get a 99.9% platform availability SLA for the reserved pool; for trials we provide the same operational controls but without an SLA credit. Planned maintenance windows are communicated with 72h notice; unplanned preemption is covered by automated fallback to a compatible hosted variant (configured via canary fallback).

Diego — attaching the SOW stub and the cost-model template I mentioned. I’ll draft a short procurement summary that NovaApps can use to justify the spend to finance.

Attachment: NovaApps_SOW_v1.pdf (PDF, 12 KB)
Related: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call with procurement if that helps.

—Marissa Cole
